title: Brits Now Track Four Health Habits a Day
paragraphs: Many people in the UK now keep a close eye on their health every day. According to a new survey, the average British adult tracks four different health habits a day.
The survey was carried out by OnePoll for the drinks brand Naked Smoothies. It asked 2,000 adults in the UK about their habits, and the results were published in October 2026.
The most common things that people track are their steps, their exercise and their sleep. Some people also track newer things, such as their breathing rate and how much fiber they eat.

Tracking has also become much more popular in recent years. Compared with about five years ago, the number of people tracking their sleep has more than doubled. The number of people tracking their steps has risen by 72%, while the number tracking how much water they drink has risen by 65%. Body weight was the only thing that people tracked less often than before.
Younger people track the most. On average, people in Gen Z and millennials track about five things, while baby boomers track fewer than three.

Why do people do it? Around 48% said they track their habits to improve their health, and 70% said that reaching their goals gives them a feeling of achievement. For many people, tracking has also changed their behavior. Among those who said it had changed their lifestyle, about half said they now walk more and drink more water.
According to the survey, people walk 7,135 steps and sleep for six and a half hours a night on average.
A doctor, Emily Jackman, said that it was encouraging to see younger people taking such an interest in their health.
